mainTopic: A husband's trick to force a Torah-level oath, orphans collecting with an oath, and collecting a כתובה or a loan while the other side is away
overview: The גמרא first shows how a clever husband can bring his wife to a שבועה דאורייתא about her כתובה. He pays the full כתובה in front of witnesses and then calls the earlier payment a loan. רב שישא בריה דרב אידי and רב אשי each find a problem with the earlier version and refine the plan, and רב אשי's version is the final one. Next the גמרא brings a משנה in שבועות that says orphans collect only with an oath, and explains that it means the lender's orphans collecting from the borrower's orphans. רב יהודה's limit on that rule is restated after רבא shows that saying 'I never borrowed' counts as saying 'I never repaid.' Then the גמרא discusses a woman collecting while her husband is away. רבי יצחק says this applies only to a כתובה, and רב נחמן says even a lender may collect this way. Finally, רבי ירמיה explains that רבי שמעון limits the heirs' oath to when she claims her כתובה, not her food support.

steps.title: The clever husband's trick: turning the first payment into a loan
steps.stepSummary: A smart husband pays her the full כתובה in front of one witness, joins that witness to the earlier one, and then claims the first payment was really a loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the husband is clever, he can bring her to a Torah-level oath. He pays her full כתובה in front of one witness, combines the first witness with this later witness, and then treats the first payment as a loan.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא describes a plan a husband can use to force his wife into a שבועה דאורייתא, instead of only a Rabbinic oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, one witness saw her receive part of her כתובה, and that only led to a lighter oath. Now he pays the whole כתובה in front of another witness, so two witnesses together cover the full payment. Then he says the first money was a loan, and a claim about a loan backed by one witness brings a Torah-level oath.

keyTerms.meaning: An oath required by Torah law

steps.confusionAlert: The husband is not denying that he paid. He is changing what the first payment was: not a כתובה payment, but a loan that she now owes him back.

phrases.english: If he is clever,
he can bring her to a Torah-level oath.
He gives her her כתובה
in front of one witness,
and joins the first witness to the last witness,
phrases.notes: The 'first witness' is the one who earlier saw her get part of her כתובה.

phrases.english: and establishes those first ones as a loan.
phrases.notes: 'Those first ones' means the money from the first payment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי פִּיקֵּחַ הוּא, מַיְיתֵי לַהּ לִידֵי שְׁבוּעָה דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of a single witness testifying that the כתובה was partly paid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A clever husband can create a Torah-level oath by paying the full כתובה before a second witness and recasting the first payment as a loan.

steps.title: How can two witnesses to different payments be combined?
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי objects: the first and last witness saw different events, so how can they be joined?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא son of רב אידי objects: How can he join the first witness to the last witness?
steps.whatsHappening: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי attacks the plan by questioning the joining of the two witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each witness saw a different payment at a different time. Since they are not testifying about the same thing, it is hard to treat them as one pair of witnesses to the full payment.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Sheisha son of Rav Idi objects to this:
How can he join the first witness
to the last witness?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי
steps.kashyaTarget: The joining of the first witness with the last witness
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two witnesses saw different payments, so their testimony cannot be combined.

steps.title: Pay her in front of both witnesses together
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא suggests the husband pay the full כתובה in front of both the first and last witness, then call the first payment a loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב שישא son of רב אידי said: He pays her full כתובה in front of both the first witness and the last witness, and then treats the first payment as a loan.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שישא fixes the problem he raised by giving a better version of the plan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both witnesses see the same full payment, so there is no need to combine separate testimonies. The first witness still saw the earlier money, which supports calling it a loan, and that leads to a Torah-level oath.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejecting the earlier idea and giving a new one)

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Sheisha son of Rav Idi said:
He gives her her כתובה
in front of the first witness and the last witness
and establishes those first ones as a loan.
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is part of the corrected wording, so read the word as להו, 'them.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the plan of step 1 to avoid the problem raised in step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The husband could combine two witnesses who each saw a different payment.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both witnesses must see the same full payment together.

steps.title: She can claim there were two כתובות
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי objects: the wife can say she had two כתובות, so both payments were real כתובה payments and not a loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי objects: She can still say, 'There were two כתובות!'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי shows that רב שישא's plan still does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband wants to say the first money was a loan. But the wife can answer that he wrote her two כתובות, and each payment was for a different one. Then there is no loan, and no oath.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi objects to this:
She can still say:
There were two כתובות!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב שישא's plan from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שישא's method of calling the first payment a loan
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wife has an easy counter-claim, that there were two כתובות, so the first payment need not be a loan.

steps.title: The husband tells the witnesses there is only one כתובה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the plan works if the husband makes the witnesses aware of what he is paying.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: He informs them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives the final fix: the husband makes a clear statement to the witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By telling the witnesses that this payment is for the one כתובה he wrote her, he blocks her claim of two כתובות. Now the first payment can only be a loan, and she must take a Torah-level oath about it.
steps.whatToRemember: Final version (רב אשי): the husband pays the full כתובה in front of both witnesses and tells them it is for his one כתובה. That turns the first payment into a loan and brings a שבועה דאורייתא.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
He informs them.
phrases.notes: He tells the witnesses that this payment is for the one כתובה he wrote her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem from step 4 and finishes the discussion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Added condition that closes a loophole
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Paying in front of both witnesses alone is enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: He must also inform the witnesses that this payment is for the one כתובה, so she cannot claim two.

steps.title: New topic: liened property, and the משנה about orphans
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the משנה's words 'from liened property' and quotes a משנה in שבועות that orphans collect only with an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'From liened property.' We learned there: And similarly, orphans collect only with an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section by quoting the next words of our משנה, then brings a related משנה from elsewhere. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה said a woman collecting her כתובה from property that was sold to others needs an oath. The גמרא now brings a משנה that also requires an oath, this time when orphans collect. The coming lines will explain that משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Liened property that was sold to someone else
We learned in a משנה elsewhere

phrases.english: "From liened property."
phrases.notes: These are words quoted from our משנה, opening a new topic.

phrases.english: We learned there:
And similarly, orphans
collect only with an oath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the husband's trick to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Orphans, like others in that משנה, can collect a debt only by taking an oath.

steps.title: From whom do the orphans collect with an oath?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the orphans in the משנה collect from. It rejects the idea that they collect from the borrower himself, because their father could have collected from him without an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: From whom do they collect only with an oath? If you say from the borrower himself, that makes no sense. Their father would take the money without an oath, so why should they need one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the משנה it just quoted: the orphans collect only with an oath, but from whom? It tests one possible answer and shows that it fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lender with a document collects from a living borrower without an oath. Orphans should not have a harder time than their father, so the משנה cannot mean they collect from the borrower himself. This pushes us toward a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (an option that the גמרא is about to reject)

phrases.english: From whom? If you say from the borrower,
phrases.notes: He means: from whom do the orphans in the משנה in שבועות collect with an oath?

phrases.english: now, their father takes without an oath,
and they need an oath?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the case of the משנה in שבועות quoted in step 6
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who are the orphans collecting from when they need an oath?
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the orphans collect from the borrower himself
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The father collects from the borrower without an oath, so his orphans should not be worse off

steps.title: It means orphans collecting from orphans
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the משנה is talking about the lender's orphans collecting from the borrower's orphans, and in that case they need an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what the משנה means: in the same way, orphans who collect from orphans may collect only with an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The case is orphans on both sides: the lender's children collecting from the borrower's children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the borrower has died, his children cannot argue for him the way he could have, so anyone collecting from orphans must swear first. The lender's orphans do not know firsthand whether the debt was repaid. So their oath is that their father never told them it was paid. That is why an oath is needed here, even though the father needed none against a living borrower.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (a rereading of the source)

phrases.english: Rather, this is what it means:
and likewise, orphans collecting from orphans
phrases.notes: The first orphans are the lender's children. The second orphans are the borrower's children.

phrases.english: may collect only with an oath.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה refers to the lender's orphans collecting from the borrower's orphans

steps.title: רב יהודה limits the oath rule
steps.stepSummary: רב זריקא quotes רב יהודה. The rule of collecting with an oath applies only when the orphans report that their father said 'I borrowed and repaid.' If he said 'I never borrowed,' they cannot collect at all, even with an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זריקא said in the name of רב יהודה: this rule was taught only when the orphans say, 'Father told us: I borrowed and paid back.' But if they say, 'Father told us: I never borrowed,' the lender's side cannot collect even with an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא sets a limit on the rule of orphans collecting with an oath. He makes the rule depend on what the dead borrower told his children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה seems to treat 'I never borrowed' as a stronger defense than 'I borrowed and repaid.' As this version tells it, that claim would block collection completely. The next step will challenge this.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this when... (a limit on a rule)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב זְרִיקָא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: Rav Zerika said that Rav Yehuda said:
They taught this only when the orphans said:
"Father told us: 'I borrowed and repaid,'"

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אָמְרוּ: אָמַר לָנוּ אַבָּא ״לֹא לָוִיתִי״ —
phrases.english: but if they said: "Father told us: 'I did not borrow,'"
they may not collect even with an oath.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב זְרִיקָא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule established in step 8
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The oath rule applies only to 'I borrowed and repaid.' With 'I did not borrow,' there is no collection even with an oath.

steps.title: רבא: saying 'I never borrowed' is like saying 'I never repaid'
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that the opposite should be true. Someone who denies ever borrowing is treated as if he admits he never repaid, so his claim should make him weaker, not stronger.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged this: Just the opposite! Anyone who says 'I never borrowed' is treated as if he said 'I never repaid.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב יהודה's statement as it was just reported. He argues that it gets the logic backwards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a man denies the loan completely and the loan is proven, he has also shown that he never paid it back. So 'I never borrowed' ruins his own defense. It should not protect his children better than 'I borrowed and repaid.'
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two claims. 'I borrowed and repaid' leaves room for a real defense. 'I never borrowed' is treated as an admission of non-payment once the loan is proven.

phrases.english: Rava challenged it: On the contrary!
Anyone who says "I did not borrow"
is considered like one who says "I did not repay."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יהודה's statement in step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's ruling that 'I did not borrow' blocks collection even with an oath
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Denying the loan is treated as admitting non-payment, so it should weaken the borrower's side, not strengthen it

steps.title: רב יהודה's statement restated the opposite way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא restates רב יהודה's teaching. If the father said 'I never borrowed,' the lender's side collects even without an oath, because that claim counts as 'I never repaid.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if this was said, it was said like this: רב זריקא said in the name of רב יהודה: the oath rule was taught only when the orphans say, 'Father told us: I borrowed and repaid.' But if they say, 'Father told us: I never borrowed,' the lender's side collects without an oath. This is because anyone who says 'I never borrowed' is like one who says 'I never repaid.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts רבא's point and fixes the report of רב יהודה's words. Now the 'I never borrowed' case is the easier one for the lender's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is the same, but the result is flipped. With 'I borrowed and repaid,' a repayment is possible, so the lender's orphans must swear. With 'I never borrowed,' the father has admitted he never paid, so no oath is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said, it was said this way (a corrected version of a statement)

steps.whatToRemember: When orphans collect from orphans, they need an oath if the dead borrower claimed 'I borrowed and repaid.' If he claimed 'I never borrowed,' they collect without an oath, because denying the loan counts as admitting he never repaid.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a basic rule of claims in court: a total denial that turns out false works against the one who made it.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was said, it was said like this:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב זְרִיקָא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Rav Zerika said that Rav Yehuda said:
They taught this only when the orphans said:
"Father told us: 'I borrowed and repaid,'"

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אָמְרוּ: אָמַר לָנוּ אַבָּא ״לֹא לָוִיתִי״ —
phrases.english: but if they said: "Father told us: 'I did not borrow,'"
they collect without an oath.
For anyone who says "I did not borrow"
is considered like one who says "I did not repay."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge in step 10 by restating רב יהודה's teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'I did not borrow' blocks collection even with an oath
steps.terutzMaskana: 'I did not borrow' lets the lender's side collect without an oath, since it is treated as 'I did not repay'
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Orphans collect from orphans with an oath only against the claim 'I borrowed and repaid.' Against 'I never borrowed,' they collect without an oath.

steps.title: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line in the משנה: a woman who collects when her husband is not present may collect only with an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who collects her כתובה when her husband is not there may collect only if she takes an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is opening a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. This sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא was talking about orphans collecting a loan. Now it moves to a different rule in the משנה: collecting שלא בפניו, meaning while the husband is away. The question the next steps will answer is how far this rule reaches.

keyTerms.meaning: not in his presence, while he is away

phrases.english: And a woman who collects not in his presence
phrases.notes: "His" means her husband's. She is collecting her כתובה while he is away.

phrases.english: may collect only with an oath.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנִפְרַעַת שֶׁלֹּא בְּפָנָיו, לֹא תִּפָּרַע אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבוּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic from the משנה after finishing the discussion of the orphans collecting with an oath.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman collecting her כתובה while her husband is away must swear in order to collect.

steps.title: רבי יצחק limits the rule to a wife's כתובה
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא שר הבירה reports a case before רבי יצחק in אנטוכיא. רבי יצחק ruled that collecting while the other side is away applies only to a כתובה, not to a regular lender.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא שר הבירה said: A case came before רבי יצחק in Antioch, and he said: This rule was taught only for a wife's כתובה, so that women would be glad to marry. A creditor does not collect this way.
steps.whatsHappening: A real case is reported. In it רבי יצחק ruled that only a wife may collect while the other side is away, and a lender may not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק sees the משנה's rule as a special benefit for women, given משום חינא, so that women will want to marry. Since it is a special benefit, it does not carry over to a בעל חוב. A lender must wait until the borrower is present, because maybe the borrower already paid.

keyTerms.meaning: they taught this only for..., which limits a rule
favor, charm. Here it means making marriage appealing to women

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a real disagreement about whether a lender can collect from an absent borrower. That question matters a great deal in practical monetary law.

phrases.english: Rav Acha, the officer of the capital, said:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֶׂה בָּא לִפְנֵי רַבִּי יִצְחָק בְּאַנְטוֹכְיָא,
phrases.english: A case came before Rabbi Yitzchak in Antioch,
and he said: They taught this only
for a wife's marriage contract,
because of favor.
phrases.notes: The idea is to make marriage appealing, so women will be glad to marry.

phrases.english: But a creditor does not.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֶׂה בָּא לִפְנֵי רַבִּי יִצְחָק בְּאַנְטוֹכְיָא, וְאָמַר: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא לִכְתוּבַּת אִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines how far the משנה's rule quoted in step 12 reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Collecting while the other side is away, with an oath, is a special enactment for a כתובה because of חינא. A creditor cannot collect from an absent borrower.

steps.title: רב נחמן says even a lender may collect
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes רב נחמן: even a lender may collect from an absent borrower with an oath, so that borrowers cannot run away overseas with the money and lenders do not stop lending.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב נחמן: Even a creditor collects this way. Otherwise anyone could take his friend's money and go live overseas. Then you would be shutting the door on people who need loans.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion disagrees with רבי יצחק. It says a lender can also collect when the borrower is away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן gives a practical reason. If a borrower could block collection just by leaving the country, people would stop lending. Then honest borrowers would be hurt. So the rule of collecting with an oath is not only a benefit for women but also protects the whole lending system.

keyTerms.meaning: locking the door in front of borrowers, meaning loans would stop

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of נועל דלת בפני לווין, not locking the door on borrowers, is a well-known reason the רבנן give for enactments that protect lenders.
steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not saying a lender collects without an oath. He agrees an oath is needed. He only disagrees about whether a lender can collect while the borrower is away.

phrases.english: And Rava said that Rav Nachman said:
Even a creditor collects this way,
so that it should not be that each and every person
takes his friend's money
and goes and settles overseas,
and you would be locking the door in front of borrowers.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: אֲפִילּוּ בַּעַל חוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יצחק in step 13 by extending the rule to a creditor.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A creditor may also collect with an oath from an absent borrower, so that lending does not stop.

steps.title: Which line of the משנה is רבי שמעון responding to?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון's words in the משנה and asks which earlier statement he is responding to.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: Whenever she demands her כתובה, and so on. Which statement in the משנה is רבי שמעון responding to?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון from the משנה and asks which earlier line his words are aimed at. This sets up רבי ירמיה's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's words sound like a reaction to something earlier in the משנה, but it is not clear which line. To understand what he adds or disagrees with, we first need to know what he is reacting to.

keyTerms.meaning: on which one? Which statement does this refer to?
and so on, meaning the rest of the quote

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Whenever she demands her marriage contract, and so on.
Which statement is Rabbi Shimon referring to?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line in the משנה after the disagreement over creditors.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which earlier ruling in the משנה is רבי שמעון reacting to?

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: רבי שמעון responds to the oath rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה explains that רבי שמעון is responding to the line about collecting while the husband is away. That line requires an oath for both food support and the כתובה. רבי שמעון comes to say the heirs make her swear only when she demands her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: He is responding to this line: A woman who collects when he is not there may collect only with an oath. That line makes no difference between food support and the כתובה. רבי שמעון comes to say that only when she demands her כתובה do the heirs make her swear.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers the question. רבי שמעון is reacting to the oath rule quoted earlier, and he narrows it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion in the משנה requires an oath whether she is taking מזונות (food support) or her כתובה. רבי שמעון says the heirs make her swear only when she demands her כתובה. This implies that when she only takes food support, she does not swear.

keyTerms.meaning: on this one, referring to this statement
food support, the widow's living expenses
they make someone take an oath

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יצחק says only a wife can collect while the other side is away. רב נחמן says a lender can too, so lending does not stop. רבי שמעון narrows the oath so that the heirs make her swear only when she claims her כתובה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said: He refers to this:
And a woman who collects not in his presence
may collect only with an oath.
It makes no difference whether it is for food support
or for the marriage contract.
And Rabbi Shimon comes to say:
whenever she demands her marriage contract,
the heirs make her take an oath.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון is reacting to the oath rule for collecting while the husband is away. He limits the oath to when she claims her כתובה, not when she only takes food support.
